label: Mandatory Programmable volume fee
summary: Preserve the inclusive 0.1 percent Programmable share on executed canonical swap or fill volume across the project's actual settlement design.
requiredFacts: Whether the project declares any Programmable-canonical execution scope; zero scopes means an empty applicability proof without inventing a token, pool, hook or fee instance
For every applicable Programmable-canonical execution scope, the effective total is the greater of the selected fee and 10 basis points
For every applicable Programmable-canonical execution scope, exactly 10 basis points belongs to 0x4957f49620AFf3Adbbe8195a4f633E49cc93376c and the remainder belongs to the project
Every Programmable-canonical execution scope and its actual standard-AMM, zero-AMM, async/batched or custom-reviewed collection profile
The executed gross quote-side basis for every applicable swap direction, exactness mode, partial fill and settlement path
Rounding, carry, dust, funding, custody and same-hook PoolManager-call behavior
Scope-isolated liabilities and immutable owner-only claims to a selected nonzero per-claim destination
requiredFiles: For zero canonical scopes, an explicit applicability record with empty scopes and no fabricated fee-policy instance
For every canonical scope, fee-enforcing hook or settlement source
For every canonical scope, a Fee V2 policy instance, selected collection profiles and worked examples
For every canonical scope, profile-specific fee accounting, custody, claim and reconstruction evidence
requiredTests: Zero-scope projects prove that no Programmable-canonical execution path exists and do not fabricate fee behavior
Applicable scopes prove the ten-basis-point floor and non-additive split
Applicable scopes cover every direction, exactness mode, fill path, split execution and cancellation or refund path
Applicable scopes cover lifetime rounding carry, dust, partial fills and self-call policy
Applicable scopes prove immutable owner-only claims, arbitrary safe per-claim destination, and no bypass, double collection, cross-scope netting or liability leakage
risks: Incorrect executed gross-volume basis can overcharge, undercharge or collect twice
Rounding, batching and partial fills can break exact conservation
Mutable or shared claim authority can redirect accrued fees
